nodes.label: The Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
nodes.author: Alex Iacob, Andrej Jovanović, William F. Shen, Daniel Burkhardt, Meghdad Kurmanji, Nurbek Tastan, Lorenzo Sani, Niccolò Alberto Elia Venanzi, Ambroise Odonnat, Zeyu Cao, Bill Marino, Xinchi Qiu, Nicholas D. Lane
nodes.rationale: Self-improving agents assume stationary evaluation criteria, but biological evolution shows species adapt to co-evolving competitors. This work extends recursive self-improvement to non-stationary utilities through co-evolved evaluators.

nodes.label: Red Queen Gödel Machine (RQGM)
nodes.rationale: Core framework enabling co-evolution of agents and evaluators through controlled utility evolution, organizing search into epochs with fixed within-epoch evaluation but evolving objectives across epochs.

nodes.label: Controlled Utility Evolution
nodes.rationale: Mechanism dividing search into evolutionary epochs with fixed evaluation within each epoch but allowing utility changes at epoch boundaries, enabling non-stationary objectives while preserving per-epoch convergence guarantees.

nodes.label: Selective Erasure
nodes.rationale: Procedure removing only utility records dependent on a replaced evaluator at epoch boundaries, preserving epoch-local stationarity and enabling evaluator replacement without violating fixed-criterion search guarantees.

nodes.label: Clade Metaproductivity (CMP)
nodes.rationale: Search utility scoring nodes by success rate pooled over their clade (subtree of descendants) rather than individual performance, capturing long-run self-improvement value beyond immediate benchmark scores.

nodes.label: Huxley-Gödel Machine (HGM)
nodes.rationale: Prior self-improvement framework using archive search guided by clade metaproductivity; RQGM extends HGM to support non-stationary utilities while preserving its per-epoch convergence guarantees.

nodes.label: HyperAgents
nodes.rationale: Self-improvement system introducing metacognitive workspaces where each archive node contains multiple role agents plus a meta-agent that edits code; RQGM builds on this multi-agent workspace architecture.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Workspace
nodes.rationale: Each archive node contains K role agents (task agents and evaluators) plus a meta-agent, enabling co-evolution where shared code expansions improve multiple utilities simultaneously.

nodes.label: Learned Evaluators
nodes.rationale: Agentic evaluators that improve alongside task agents they score, enabling evaluation in domains without objective benchmarks and providing complementary signals where ground truth exists.

nodes.label: Evaluator-Dependent Roles
nodes.rationale: Task roles (e.g., paper writing, proof writing) lacking ground-truth signals, requiring learned evaluators scored against held-out ground-truth anchors for replacement decisions.

nodes.label: Evaluator-Independent Roles
nodes.rationale: Task roles with fixed benchmarks (e.g., coding with executable tests), providing objective evaluation signals independent of learned evaluators.

nodes.label: Ground-Truth Anchor
nodes.rationale: Fixed held-out dataset of objective or human-preference labels used to evaluate and select learned evaluators at epoch boundaries, providing evaluator-independent replacement criterion.

nodes.label: ε-Best-Belief Score
nodes.rationale: Conservative lower bound (ε-quantile of Beta posterior) used for both final agent selection and evaluator replacement, ensuring promoted evaluators exceed incumbent with probability 1-ε.

nodes.label: Polyglot Coding Domain
nodes.rationale: Experimental domain with verifiable ground truth (executable tests) where RQGM co-evolves a code reviewer alongside the coder, achieving 1.35×–1.72× token efficiency over HGM-H baseline.

nodes.label: Paper Writing Domain
nodes.rationale: Experimental domain without objective benchmark where RQGM co-evolves writers with learned reviewers, achieving 1.78×–1.86× higher acceptance rates over HGM-H on fixed reviewer panel.

nodes.label: Proof Writing Domain
nodes.rationale: Experimental domain (IMO Olympiad proofs) where RQGM co-evolves provers with learned graders, achieving higher panel-mean scores and Pass@6 rates over longer horizons than HGM-H.

nodes.label: Adversarial Objective
nodes.rationale: Search intervention correcting LLM self-preference bias by introducing adversarial pool of AI-generated papers accepted by displaced reviewer, rewarding future reviewers for rejecting them equally with human papers.

nodes.label: Curriculum-Like Effect
nodes.rationale: Progressively stricter evaluators across epochs impose curriculum on task agents, with each replacement re-ranking archive and advancing population around resilient backbone lineages.

nodes.label: Thompson Sampling
nodes.rationale: Exploration-exploitation strategy used to select nodes for expansion/evaluation by sampling from Beta posterior over clade metaproductivity, balancing discovery against exploitation.

nodes.label: UCB-Air Expansion Gate
nodes.rationale: Mechanism controlling archive growth by deciding whether to expand or evaluate based on relationship between evaluation budget and archive size, preventing unbounded tree growth.

nodes.label: Checkpoint Schedule
nodes.rationale: Exponentially-spaced checkpoints where evaluator replacements occur, bounding cumulative re-evaluation cost to O(B) rather than O(B²) over total budget B.

nodes.label: Data Isolation
nodes.rationale: Separation of training data (shown to meta-agent for guidance) from validation data (used for search utility), preventing overfitting and ensuring generalization.

nodes.label: Three-Level Sampling Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical sampling selecting nodes by CMP, then roles by least-evaluated, then tasks by least-evaluated, ensuring balanced evaluation across roles and tasks within each node.

nodes.label: Proposition 1: Working-Posterior Consistency
nodes.rationale: Theoretical result showing pooled Beta accumulator converges to role-task balanced utility under balanced sampling, preserving HGM's flat success/failure interface for Thompson sampling.

nodes.label: Proposition 3: Epoch-Local Fixed-Criterion Validity
nodes.rationale: Core theoretical result establishing each epoch as fixed-criterion binary-outcome search problem, enabling direct application of HGM convergence guarantees within epochs.

nodes.label: Proposition 6: Bounded Recovery
nodes.rationale: Theoretical result bounding cumulative re-evaluation cost of evaluator replacements to O(B) with exponentially-spaced checkpoints, preventing asymptotic overhead.

nodes.label: LLM Self-Preference Bias
nodes.rationale: Known weakness of LLM judges favoring AI-generated text; RQGM corrects this through adversarial objectives, discovering reviewers equally stringent on machine and human work.

nodes.label: Specialist vs. Generalist Selection
nodes.rationale: Two selection strategies: specialist maximizes best-belief on single target utility, generalist maximizes average across active utilities, showing whether improvements come from task-specific or joint optimization.

nodes.label: Blended Token Cost Metric
nodes.rationale: Cost accounting combining input and output tokens with output weighted 5× input, enabling fair comparison across models with different input/output cost ratios.

nodes.label: GPT-5.5 (low)
nodes.rationale: Primary foundation model used for all main experiments, selected for cost-intelligence trade-off; meta-agent and final evaluation use this model.

nodes.label: Nemotron 3 Ultra
nodes.rationale: Efficient foundation model used in cost-reduction ablation for search-time task-agent calls, achieving 13.0× lower search cost while approaching GPT-5.5 accuracy.

nodes.label: APReS Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Conference paper acceptance/rejection dataset used as ground-truth anchor for paper-review domain, enabling evaluator replacement decisions.

nodes.label: IMO-GradingBench
nodes.rationale: Human-graded IMO proof dataset used as ground-truth anchor for proof-grading domain, enabling evaluator replacement decisions.

nodes.label: CRAVE Dataset
nodes.rationale: Code review dataset of accepted/rejected pull requests used as ground-truth anchor for code-review evaluator in Polyglot domain.

nodes.label: Van Valen's Red Queen Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Biological principle that species adapt to maintain fitness relative to co-evolving competitors; motivates RQGM's co-evolutionary approach to self-improvement.

nodes.label: Gödel Machine
nodes.rationale: Theoretical self-improving system that modifies itself whenever it can prove changes beneficial; RQGM makes this empirical through archive search with co-evolved evaluators.

nodes.label: Darwin-Gödel Machine (DGM)
nodes.rationale: Prior empirical self-improvement system ranking self-modifying coding agents by benchmark utility; baseline for comparison in coding domain.

nodes.label: Open-Endedness
nodes.rationale: Goal of generating novel artifacts indefinitely; RQGM enables this by co-evolving objectives, allowing search to bootstrap evaluation beyond static benchmarks.

nodes.label: Reward Hacking
nodes.rationale: Problem where agents exploit static benchmarks; RQGM mitigates through co-evolved evaluators that harden over time, making objectives harder to hack.

nodes.label: RQ1: Benefits When Ground Truth Exists
nodes.rationale: Research question validating that co-evolved learned evaluation improves search efficiency even on verifiable tasks where ground truth exists.

nodes.label: RQ2: Learned Evaluation Without Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Research question validating that co-evolved agents outperform fixed-evaluator baselines in domains with no objective benchmark.

nodes.label: RQ3: Evaluator Replacements as Curriculum
nodes.rationale: Research question examining whether evaluator replacements drive curriculum-like search by re-ranking archive while preserving backbone lineages.

nodes.label: RQ4: Co-Evolution Improves Evaluators
nodes.rationale: Research question validating that same dynamics improving generators also improve evaluators, with co-evolved grader reaching higher accuracy at lower cost.

nodes.label: Assumption 1: HGM-Compatible Fixed-Criterion Search
nodes.rationale: Foundational assumption for RQGM theory: fixed evaluator, time-homogeneous outcomes, external oracles, and fixed budget accounting enable HGM guarantees within epochs.

nodes.label: Assumption 2: Stationary Learned Evaluation Within Epoch
nodes.rationale: Key assumption enabling epoch-local stationarity: evaluator, artifact generation, and scoring rule are frozen throughout each epoch.

nodes.label: Definition F.1: Criterion-Valid Record
nodes.rationale: Formal definition of utility evidence records valid under current criterion vector, enabling selective erasure to maintain criterion consistency across epochs.

nodes.label: Definition F.2: Utility Transition
nodes.rationale: Formal definition of evaluator replacement procedure: advancing epoch index, replacing criterion, and applying selective erasure to maintain criterion consistency.

nodes.label: Remark 1: Commuting Transitions on Disjoint Slots
nodes.rationale: Theoretical result showing multiple evaluator replacements on independent slots commute, enabling simultaneous replacements without order dependence.

nodes.label: Remark 3: Anchor Lower Bound
nodes.rationale: Theoretical result establishing promoted evaluator's ε-best-belief score as lower bound it exceeds with probability 1-ε, ensuring likely improvement across epochs.

nodes.label: Remark 7: Amortized Utility-Transition Cost
nodes.rationale: Theoretical result showing re-evaluation of old nodes after replacement is amortized through three-level sampling hierarchy, avoiding O(B²) cost.

nodes.label: Algorithm 1: Red Queen Gödel Machine Search
nodes.rationale: Complete pseudocode for RQGM procedure: initialization, CMP-guided search between checkpoints, evaluator replacement at checkpoints, and endpoint selection.

nodes.label: Figure 1: Polyglot Results
nodes.rationale: Empirical results showing RQGM exceeds HGM-H pass rate at 1.35×–1.72× lower token cost through co-evolved code reviewer.

nodes.label: Figure 3: Evaluator Replacements Re-Rank Archive
nodes.rationale: Empirical evidence that evaluator replacements substantially and permanently re-rank archive, with Spearman ρ settling well below 1, showing curriculum effect.

nodes.label: Figure 4: Backbone Lineage Preservation
nodes.rationale: Empirical evidence that best lineage survives evaluator replacements intact while remainder is re-ranked, showing curriculum advances around stable backbone.

nodes.label: Figure 5: Co-Evolved Grader Results
nodes.rationale: Empirical results showing co-evolved grader reaches best IMO-GradingBench accuracy at 3× lower search cost than HGM-H.

nodes.label: Figure 6: Adversarial Reviewer Results
nodes.rationale: Empirical results showing adversarial RQGM reviewer accepts AI and human papers at similar rates, correcting self-preference bias while driving strongest writer.

nodes.label: Figure 7: Cost Reduction via Hybrid Models
nodes.rationale: Ablation showing Nemotron 3 Ultra task-agent calls reduce search cost 13.0× while approaching GPT-5.5 accuracy under same final evaluation.

nodes.label: Table 1: Paper Writer Results
nodes.rationale: Empirical results showing co-evolved writers achieve 1.78×–1.86× higher acceptance rates over HGM-H on fixed reviewer panel.

nodes.label: Table 2: Proof Prover Results
nodes.rationale: Empirical results showing co-evolved specialist prover attains best mean score and Pass@6 rate, exceeding HGM-H and approaching IMO25 baseline.

nodes.label: Table 7: Mechanism Ablations
nodes.rationale: Ablation study isolating components: replacement alone escapes saturation, erasure prevents stale utility, adversarial pool refines decision boundary.

nodes.label: Listing 1: Diff-Hygiene Repair
nodes.rationale: Code patch discovered by meta-agent filtering untracked dependency artifacts and unsafe symlinks, load-bearing improvement in Polyglot winning chain.

nodes.label: Listing 2: Revision Retraction
nodes.rationale: Code patch discovered by meta-agent disabling self-revision by default, preserving sound detailed proofs over weaker black-box citations.

nodes.label: Future Work: Longer Search Horizons
nodes.rationale: Acknowledged limitation: current investigation uses short search horizons; longer co-evolution expected to compound curriculum effects and extend improvement beyond static benchmarks.

nodes.label: Limitation: Anchor Quality Dependence
nodes.rationale: Acknowledged limitation: evaluator quality bounded by anchor quality; weak or biased anchor yields uninformative evaluators.

nodes.label: Limitation: Epoch-Local Guarantees
nodes.rationale: Acknowledged limitation: theoretical guarantees are epoch-local, covering improvement only within epochs, not across epoch boundaries.

nodes.label: Controlled Utility Evolution in RQGM
nodes.rationale: Describes slot-m replacement rule, best-belief lower-bound trajectory, and piecewise fixed-criterion validity for evaluator evolution

nodes.label: Best-Belief Lower-Bound Trajectory
nodes.rationale: Calibration statement about selected lower-bound trajectory; justifies interpreting increasing best-belief curve as increasing posterior evidence for better agents

nodes.label: Piecewise Fixed-Criterion Validity
nodes.rationale: Epoch-local result: after conditioning on checkpoint decision and applying selective erasure, each realized epoch is compatible with fixed-criterion binary-outcome interface

nodes.label: Evaluator Anchor Lower Bound at Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: Per-checkpoint lower-bound statement; evaluator slot is fixed-criterion selection sampled at checkpoints because replacement test scored only on fixed anchor

nodes.label: Exponential Checkpoint Overhead with Linear Work
nodes.rationale: Total reprocessed records over exponential checkpoints is O(B) with constant at most ρ/(ρ-1); base-two schedule yields bound of at most 2B

nodes.label: Anchor Weakness Risk in Evaluator Evolution
nodes.rationale: Weak, noisy, or biased anchor allows evaluators to drift across epochs; particularly problematic since APReS decisions and IMO-GradingBench grades are imperfect

nodes.label: Epoch-Local Theoretical Guarantees
nodes.rationale: Theoretical guarantees for RQGM are inherently localized and constrained; do not bound transition counts, cumulative regret, or long-term convergence

nodes.label: Calibration Assumption in Working Posterior
nodes.rationale: Working posterior is mean-consistent only; calibration assumption cannot strictly hold in real-world deployments due to systemic volatility

nodes.label: Stationary Learned-Evaluation Condition
nodes.rationale: Within each epoch, evaluator-dependent roles satisfy stationary learned-evaluation condition; cannot strictly hold due to provider-side model updates and nondeterministic tools
